text:
Alex C (CS): hey team — client sent a production alert: our rerank endpoint returned negative, non-normalized scores and their downstream service treats them as probabilities so rankings collapsed. they hit this in a nightly job after a model rotation. request id: req_0a1b2c3d

Tasha S (Support): thanks for the heads up, alex. can you paste a redacted request/response? also which model and endpoint?

Alex C (CS): pasted below (redacted):

```
POST /v1/rerank
Payload: {"query":"best running shoes","candidates":["shoe A","shoe B","shoe C"], "top_k":3}
Response: {"scores":[-2.31, 0.12, -0.55], "candidates":[...], "model":"redwood-rerank-v2"}
```

Alex C (CS): client expected [0..1] probs. they did softmax previously, but their wrapper assumed api returns normalized probs. they saw negative values and interpreted as ties -> exploded downstream metric.

Sam R (ML): quick context: our reranker returns raw scoring logits by design (unbounded), because we let customers choose downstream transforms (softmax, sigmoid, pairwise margin). negative values are expected and do not indicate error.

Morgan E (Eng): tagging docs/SDK: @Sam — can we add an explicit field or flag to the API to optionally return normalized scores? client impact looks high.

Sam R (ML): short-term: advise client to run softmax across candidate set to get normalized probabilities. if they want per-candidate independent scores, use sigmoid. example:
```
softmax = exp(scores) / sum(exp(scores))
```

Jordan P (PM): we should proactively surface this in the API docs + quickstart. also consider a compatibility param `normalize=true|false` for hosted API so naive integrations don't break.

Tasha S (Support): shared repro steps for client: please try this locally and confirm identical behavior, include request id and timestamps:
1) call rerank with same candidate ordering
2) apply softmax across returned scores
3) verify top-k matches expected ordering

Alex C (CS): did that and ordering is stable after softmax, just the absolute numbers changed. client wants a rollback to previous model variant that returned non-negative range (they relied on that).

Morgan E (Eng): note: returning normalized probs on the server has pitfalls for batching across requests of varying candidate counts. we'll need to normalize per-request, not per-batch, and ensure consistent float stability. potential perf hit but doable as opt-in.

Sam R (ML): logging note: the raw logits let you compare margins; negative is fine. also pros/cons for docs: explain when to use raw vs normalized and include example code for Python/JS.

Alex C (CS): client asked for immediate mitigation — they can patch with softmax in their pipeline, but want us to flag this in release notes.

Morgan E (Eng): action items: @Sam draft docs blurb + code snippets; @Jordan evaluate `normalize` flag spec; @Eng-runtime (cc: deploy-bot) estimate perf impact for on-the-fly normalization as an opt-in param.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for eng-runtime: feature/normalize-flag — CI checks running (build 7821).

Tasha S (Support): I'll reply to client with repro + softmax snippet and offer to help with a quick code patch. will include timeline for docs and product follow-up.

Jordan P (PM): capture this as a docs + product ticket. priority P2 for SDK quick fix, P1 for explicit release note and customer comms.

Alex C (CS): thanks — I'll keep thread updated with client response. for record, client id: redacted-corp-42.

Sam R (ML): for support reply, suggested text: "The rerank API returns raw (unbounded) scores/logits by default. If you need probabilities, apply softmax across the returned candidate scores; see snippet. We're adding a compatibility opt-in flag to return normalized probabilities in future releases."

Tasha S (Support): sending now. :thumbsup:

Morgan E (Eng): adding a short note to changelog draft so the rotation notes mention score semantics.

Alex C (CS): closing loop when client confirms patch. thanks all :)
